verses.1:1: The burden concerning Nineveh: the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.1:2: A jealous and avenging God is the LORD; the LORD avenges and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His adversaries, and He keeps wrath for His enemies.
verses.1:3: The LORD is slow to anger and great in might, and He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD has His way in the whirlwind and in the tempest, and the clouds are the dust of His feet.
verses.1:4: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and He parches all the rivers; Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon languishes.
verses.1:5: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth heaves at His presence, indeed, the world and all who dwell in it.
verses.1:6: Who can stand before His indignation, and who can endure the fierceness of His anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered by Him.
verses.1:7: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; and He knows those who take refuge in Him.
verses.1:8: But with an overflowing flood He will make an utter end of her place, and He will pursue His enemies into darkness.
verses.1:9: What do you devise against the LORD? He will bring utter destruction; affliction shall not rise up a second time.
verses.1:10: For though they are entangled like thorns, and drenched as with their drink, they shall be devoured like stubble that is completely dry.
verses.1:11: From you has gone forth one who plots evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
verses.1:12: Thus says the LORD: "Though they are at full strength and likewise numerous, even so they shall be cut down, and he shall pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
verses.1:13: And now I will break his yoke from upon you, and tear your bonds apart."
verses.1:14: And the LORD has issued a command concerning you: "No longer shall any of your name be sown; from the house of your gods I will cut off the carved image and the molten image. I will prepare your grave, for you are vile."
verses.2:1: Behold, upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good tidings, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah, fulfill your vows; for the wicked one shall never again pass through you; he is utterly cut off.
verses.2:2: The scatterer has come up against your face! Guard the rampart, watch the road, fortify the loins, make your strength exceedingly firm!
verses.2:3: For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob, like the majesty of Israel; for the ravagers have emptied them out and ruined their vine branches.
verses.2:4: The shield of his mighty men is dyed red, the men of valor are clad in scarlet; the chariots gleam with fiery steel in the day of his preparation, and the cypress spears are brandished.
verses.2:5: The chariots race madly through the streets, they rush to and fro in the broad squares; their appearance is like blazing torches, they dart about like lightning.
verses.2:6: He summons his nobles; they stumble in their march. They hasten to her wall, and the protective shelter is set in place.
verses.2:7: The gates of the rivers are flung open, and the palace melts away.
verses.2:8: It is decreed: she is stripped bare, she is carried away; and her maidservants moan like the voice of doves, beating upon their breasts.
verses.2:9: Nineveh has been like a pool of water from of old, yet they are fleeing away. "Stand! Stand!"—yet no one turns back.
verses.2:10: Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, wealth from every precious vessel.
verses.2:11: Desolate, empty, and laid waste! Hearts melt and knees tremble, anguish seizes all loins, and the faces of them all turn pale.
verses.2:12: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked, along with the lion's cub, and none made them afraid?
verses.2:13: The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses; he filled his caves with prey and his dens with torn flesh.
verses.2:14: "Behold, I am against you," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will burn her chariots in smoke, and the sword shall devour your young lions; I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers shall be heard no more."
verses.3:1: Woe to the city of bloodshed! She is wholly filled with deceit and plunder; prey never departs.
verses.3:2: The crack of the whip and the rattle of the wheel, the galloping steed and the bounding chariot!
verses.3:3: Horsemen charging, the flash of the sword and the glitter of the spear, a multitude of the slain and a great heap of carcasses! There is no end to the dead bodies, and they stumble over their corpses.
verses.3:4: Because of the multitude of the harlotries of the harlot, fair and alluring, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her harlotries and families through her sorceries.
verses.3:5: "Behold, I am against you," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will uncover your skirts over your face; I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your disgrace.
verses.3:6: I will cast abominable filth upon you, treat you with contempt, and set you as a spectacle.
verses.3:7: And it shall come to pass that all who look upon you will flee from you and say, 'Nineveh is laid waste! Who will bemoan her?' Where shall I seek comforters for you?"
verses.3:8: Are you better than No-Amon, that sat among the rivers, with waters all around her, whose rampart was the sea, and whose wall was of the sea?
verses.3:9: Cush was her strength, and Egypt also, without limit; Put and the Lubim were your helpers.
verses.3:10: Yet even she went into exile, into captivity; her little ones also were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
verses.3:11: You also shall become drunken; you shall be hidden away. You also shall seek a stronghold from the enemy.
verses.3:12: All your fortresses are fig trees with first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.3:13: Behold, your people in your midst are women! The gates of your land are opened wide to your enemies; fire has devoured your bars.
verses.3:14: Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses! Go into the clay and tread the mortar, take hold of the brick mold!
verses.3:15: There the fire shall devour you, the sword shall cut you off; it shall consume you like the creeping locust. Multiply yourself like the creeping locust, multiply yourself like the swarming locust!
verses.3:16: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the heavens; the creeping locust plunders and flies away.
verses.3:17: Your princes are like the swarming locusts, and your marshals like clouds of grasshoppers that settle on the stone walls on a cold day; when the sun rises, they flee away, and their place is not known, where they are.
verses.3:18: Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; your nobles lie at rest. Your people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
verses.3:19: There is no alleviation for your injury; your wound is grievous. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over you, for upon whom has your wickedness not passed continually?

notes.1:3: The qere reads the construct form ugdol-koach, meaning great in might, whereas the ketiv reads the full spelling ugdol without construct shortening.
notes.1:10: The Hebrew wording is famously terse, picturing Assyria's defenders as hopelessly tangled like thorns and sodden with drink, yet instantly consumed like dry stubble.
notes.2:1: In Masoretic versification, chapter 2 begins here, corresponding to 1:15 in many English versions. The qere shortens the infinitive before the maqqef hyphen without changing the sense to pass through.
notes.2:4: The Hebrew term peladot is a rare word denoting steel or iron chariot fittings, and beroshim, literally cypresses, poetically refers to cypress-shafted spears.
notes.2:6: The qere reads the singular bahalikhatam, in their march, whereas the ketiv reads the plural form, in their marches or courses.
notes.2:8: The Hebrew wehutzzav is rendered here as a passive verb meaning It is decreed; some interpreters take it instead as a proper name or royal title, Huzzab.
notes.2:14: The Masoretic Text reads her chariots with a third-person feminine suffix, a poetic shift of person amidst the direct second-person address to Nineveh.
notes.3:3: The qere reads wekhashelu, and they stumble, continuing the description with a prefixed conjunction, whereas the ketiv reads yikkashelu, they stumble.
notes.3:8: No-Amon is the Hebrew name for Thebes, the famed capital of Upper Egypt straddling the Nile and its canals, which fell to Assyria in 663 BC.
notes.3:9: The Masoretic Text reads your helpers with a second-person feminine suffix, momentarily addressing No-Amon directly before returning to third-person narration in verse 10.
